title: Gutterpress Manifest
description: Configuration file for Gutterpress markdown-to-PDF converter. Mirrors the GutterpressManifest interface in packages/cli/src/schema/manifest.types.ts. Every field is optional — an absent field falls back to the resolved preset default (see packages/cli/src/lib/presets.ts).

title.description: Document title. Used for the HTML <title> and PDF metadata.

language.description: The book's language as a BCP 47 tag. It is the lang of the built HTML, which hyphenation follows, and sets the quotation marks straight quotes print as.

preset.description: How the book is designed (ADR 0008): the base defaults for every other section — page geometry, ink limits, PDF/X settings, validation checks — all overridable field-by-field below. "dtrpg" = DriveThruRPG print-on-demand (the product default when omitted); "book" = neutral 6x9in trade book; "custom" = you supply page.width and page.height yourself (required).

targets.description: Where the book is published (ADR 0008): publish targets whose requirements `gutterpress validate` checks the built PDF against — each target is validated separately, so one book can target several destinations. Omitting it uses the preset's default (dtrpg -> ["dtrpg"]; book/custom -> []).

styles.description: Project-relative CSS files to <link> into the rendered book, applied in order. If omitted, Gutterpress discovers one: styles/book.css (what `gutterpress new` scaffolds), else the first .css file found in the project root, styles/ or css/, else none. New projects should set this explicitly or use styles/book.css.

items.description: Path to a CSS file, relative to the manifest directory.

extensions.description: Extensions, in load order: markdown-it plugins, looks (stylesheets), component libraries — anything from npm or a folder. Each entry is a specifier: a bundled name (a markdown feature: markdown-it-mark, markdown-it-sub, markdown-it-sup, markdown-it-abbr, gutterpress-gfm-alerts, gutterpress-math; or a built-in look: clean-book, zine, technical-doc, academic), a path starting with ./ or ../ (relative to this file), or an npm package name, optionally pinned as name@version. A later entry loads later: its markdown runs after earlier entries' and its CSS wins ties. The project's own `styles` always load after every extension.

oneOf.description: The specifier. Bundled names resolve to the copy compiled into Gutterpress; ./ and ../ are paths relative to this file; anything else is an npm package, name@version pins it.
The object form, for an entry that needs more than its specifier. `use` carries the same specifier the bare form would.

use.description: The specifier — exactly what the bare string form would be.

export.description: Named module export to use as the markdown-it plugin function when the package has no default export.

options.description: Options passed straight through to the markdown-it plugin.

enabled.description: Per-project enable flag. Absent or true = active. false keeps the entry in the manifest (so the toggle is reversible) but skips loading it at build and preview time.

chapters.description: The book's markdown files, in reading order, relative to the manifest directory. Omit it (or set it to null) to use every top-level .md file in natural order. Book setup > Details in the app edits it. Assets are not listed anywhere: the build copies exactly what the book references.

checks.description: Per-check and per-rule levels, keyed by a check id (pdf.print.image-resolution, source.markdownlint, …) or a lint rule id (printsafe/no-risky-print-effects). `off` switches it off; `on` switches on a check the preset leaves off, at its own severity; `info`, `warn` and `error` set the severity its findings are reported at. The numbers the checks measure against come from the preset and the publish targets. Linter config files (.markdownlint.yaml, .htmlhintrc, .gutterpress/css-contract.yaml) are found by name in the book's folder or a folder above it, up to the repository.

pdfx.description: PDF/X conversion settings, used by `gutterpress build --format pdfx`.

icc.description: Path to the ICC output-intent profile, relative to the manifest directory.

stripAnnotations.description: Strip annotations (links, comments) during PDF/X conversion — PDF/X-1a does not permit them.

blackText.description: How near-black text is separated. `icc` converts it through the ICC profile (rich, four-colour black). `k-only` prints it on the black plate alone (100% K), which print vendors such as DriveThruRPG require for small text. Non-text black (rules, panels) is unaffected. Preset defaults: dtrpg `k-only`, book `icc`.

transparency.description: What a PDF/X build does with a page that uses transparency (an alpha-channel image, a soft `rgba()` shadow, CSS `opacity` or `mix-blend-mode`), which PDF/X (PDF 1.3) cannot represent. `flatten-page` leaves the page to Ghostscript, which rasterizes the WHOLE page: it looks right but loses the page's text and fonts. `preserve-text` flattens only the artwork to a picture (300 DPI, or `rasterDpi`) and draws the text live on top, so the page stays searchable. Text is then always the top layer (text another element covers shows through). A page whose text is translucent or blended, set in a Type 3 font (e.g. a synthetic bold or a text stroke), filled with a pattern or used as a clip, or that has a repeating or conic gradient, falls back to `flatten-page`, and so does any page listed in `flattenPages`. Set `checks: { asset.image.alpha-channel: off }` to use alpha-channel images. Same for every preset: `flatten-page`.

flattenPages.description: With `transparency: preserve-text`: pages (1-based, the numbers the build reports) left to Ghostscript's whole-page flattening even if they could be split, e.g. a page whose look depends on a cover or tint painted over its text. Page numbers move when the book reflows. Default: none.

rasterDpi.description: Resolution (DPI) of every picture made from a page that uses transparency: the whole pages Ghostscript flattens and the `preserve-text` artwork. Vector content and the book's own images are not resampled. Unset: Ghostscript's default (720) for whole pages, 300 for `preserve-text` artwork.

print.description: Page-count rules applied when the PDF is built.

signature.description: Pad the PDF with blank pages until the page count is a multiple of this. `1` means no padding. Preset defaults: dtrpg 4, book 1.

reserveLastPage.description: Guarantee the final page is a blank page added by the build (no background, no page number). When the content already fills a signature exactly, a full signature of blank pages is added. DriveThruRPG reserves the last page for printer information. Preset defaults: dtrpg true, book false. Same as `lastPage: blank`; `lastPage` wins when both are set.

lastPage.description: How the interior's last page is reserved for a printer that uses it (DriveThruRPG puts its printer information there). `blank` ends the interior on a blank page the build adds. `short-by-one` pads to one page short of a multiple of `signature` (k x signature - 1), and the printer supplies the last page. Wins over `reserveLastPage`. Not set by any preset.

page.description: Page geometry, in POINTS (1in = 72pt): the trim size the book prints at and, with `margin`, the margins. The build writes them as the `@page` rule after every stylesheet, so a `size` in a stylesheet's own `@page` is overridden (the print-safety check reports it); the `pdf.print.page-size` check compares the produced PDF against these numbers. A bleed-inclusive page size legitimately differs from the trim recorded here.

width.description: Page width in points (1in = 72pt): the trim the book prints at and what validation compares against. Preset defaults: dtrpg 621, book 432 (6in).

height.description: Page height in points (1in = 72pt): the trim the book prints at and what validation compares against. Preset defaults: dtrpg 810, book 648 (9in).

tolerance.description: Allowed deviation, in points, between the expected and the actual page size.

bleed.description: A bleed, in points, that the page width x height ALREADY CONTAINS on the top, bottom and OUTER edges (none on the binding edge) — how DriveThruRPG's interior file is cut (8.625 x 11.25in for an 8.5 x 11in book). It tells the preview's safe area & bleed overlay, the `pdf.print.safe-margins` check and pinned art where the trim is, and by itself changes nothing in the PDF. Preset default: dtrpg 9 (0.125in); book and custom none.

safe.description: The TEXT rule, in points: how far inside the trim glyphs must stay, on every edge (the binding edge too, unless `gutter` is set). For DriveThruRPG it is the "text at least 0.5in inside the trim" rule. The preview's overlay outlines it (dashed) and flags text outside it, and the `pdf.print.safe-margins` check fails a PDF whose text is closer. An image pinned to an edge (`.gp-pin`) where `artSafe` is not set sits on it; no book CSS moves it. Preset default: dtrpg 36 (0.5in), book 18 (0.25in); custom none.

artSafe.description: The ART rule, in points: how far inside the trim art that does not bleed (images, backgrounds, borders, rules) must stay on the top, bottom and OUTER edge; at the binding edge art uses `gutter`. For DriveThruRPG it is the "non-bleeding art at least 0.25in from the outside edges (0.5in at the binding)" rule. Art that runs out to the page's edge is a bleed and is not judged on that edge. The preview's overlay outlines it (dotted) and flags art outside it, the `pdf.print.safe-margins` check fails a PDF with an image closer (or one that stops in the bleed band), and an image pinned to the top, bottom or outer edge (`.gp-pin`) sits on it unless it carries `.gp-flush`. Absent = the same as `safe`. Preset default: dtrpg 18 (0.25in); book and custom none.

gutter.description: The binding allowance, in points: how far content stays from the spine, measured from the trim at the binding edge (the left edge of a right-hand page, the right edge of a left-hand one). It stands in for `safe` there, for text and for art alike: the preview's overlay draws and judges that edge against it, the `pdf.print.safe-margins` check fails text or an image closer to the spine than it, and an image pinned to the binding edge (`.gp-pin`) sits on it. The other edges keep `safe` and `artSafe`. Use it when your book keeps its text further from the spine than the printer's minimum, for example 54 (0.75in) where DriveThruRPG asks for 0.5in. Absent = the same as `safe`. Preset default: dtrpg 36 (0.5in, DriveThruRPG's rule for text and non-bleeding art at the binding — the same as its `safe`, declared so a book inherits it visibly); book and custom none.

margin.description: Page margins, in points (1in = 72pt): the space between the trim and the text on each edge. `inside` is the binding edge (the left of a right-hand page, the right of a left-hand one), `outside` the other. When set, the book prints with these margins and any `@page` margin in a stylesheet is overridden; when left out, the stylesheets' `@page` margins apply (a look's design), else 1in. Setup > Book in the app edits it. All four edges are required together.

inside.description: Binding-edge margin in points: the left of a right-hand page, the right of a left-hand one.

publish.description: Publish provider settings, keyed by the same provider id `gutterpress publish --provider <id>` takes. Non-secret configuration only — API keys and tokens are stored in the host credential store, never in this file.

local.description: A folder on this computer — where the desktop's Publish builds the book before sending it anywhere else (default: `dist` inside the book)

dir.description: Output folder, relative to the book or absolute. Default: dist

target.description: itch.io project as user/game (the butler push target)

credential.description: Label of the saved credential to use when more than one is stored for this provider. Not a secret — just a reference into the host credential store. Empty or absent uses the default credential.

drivethrurpg.description: DriveThruRPG guided publishing (export package + open the publisher hub)

productUrl.description: Existing product page URL, when updating a published title

kdp.description: Amazon KDP guided publishing (export package + open kdp.amazon.com)

azure-swa.description: Azure Static Web Apps deployment of the HTML export

credential.description: Label of the saved credential to use when more than one is stored for this provider.

productId.description: Existing product GID/id to update instead of creating a new one

credential.description: Label of the saved credential to use when more than one is stored for this provider.

gdrive.description: Google Drive publishing (uploads the finished PDF or zipped HTML export to a Drive folder)

folder.description: Drive folder name to find-or-create at My Drive root. Ignored once folderId is recorded.

folderId.description: Stable Drive folder id to upload into, picker-set in the desktop app or hand-recorded from the CLI's post-publish tip. Takes precedence over folder when present and the folder still exists.

credential.description: Label of the saved credential to use when more than one Google account is connected. Not a secret — just a reference into the host credential store. Empty or absent uses the default credential.
